newsitem.title: USA: "Doonesbury" portrayal of drug raid irks official.
newsitem.headline: "Doonesbury" portrayal of drug raid irks official.

text.p: California's top law enforcement official is not amused by "Doonesbury" comic strip episodes poking fun at a raid by narcotics agents on a San Francisco club that said it supplied marijuana to sick people.

State Attorney General Dan Lungren called on Universal Press Syndicate, which distributes Garry Trudeau's cartoon strip, and California newspapers on Tuesday to "pull the plug" on this week's "Doonesbury" strips, Lungren's office said.
Lungren urged the step because of what his office called the strip's "inaccurate portrayal" of the San Francisco Cannabis Buyers' Club.

"While I have no authority to keep the destructive messages of this week's 'Doonesbury' from publication, you do," Lungren, a Republican who takes a tough law-and-order line, wrote in a letter to the syndicate and to several newspapers that carry the strip.

"Alternatively -- given the fact that the strips are premised on false and misleading information -- your organisation should consider running a disclaimer side-by-side with the strips which states the known facts related to the Cannabis Buyers' Club," he wrote.

The Cannabis Buyers' Club, operating in defiance of laws against marijuana possession, supplied the drug to about 12,000 San Franciscans, who the club said used marijuana to ease suffering caused by illnesses such as AIDS, cancer and glaucoma.
Drug agents from the California Department of Justice, which is headed by Lungren, closed the club on Aug. 4.

The attorney general's office said the club was "in fact a major drug distribution centre for the city of San Francisco." It said undercover videotapes had revealed that the club routinely sold marijuana to children and to people with forged doctor's notes or no medical excuse at all.
Californians will vote in November on a proposal to make it legal for sick people to use marijuana for medical purposes. Lungren adamantly opposes the measure.

In Tuesday's "Doonesbury," Zonker Harris asks a friend who ordered the raid. "Dan Lungren, the state attorney general. The local cops wouldn't do it, so they had to bring in Republicans," the friend answers.
In the raid, agents seized more than 150 pounds of marijuana and more than 400 marijuana plants, Lungren's office said. No arrests were made, but the investigation goes on, it said.
Lee Salem, editorial director of Universal Press Syndicate, based in Kansas City, Missouri, said the syndicate did not plan to withdraw the strips or provide a disclaimer.
